newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rebound, seen dipping on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rebound, seen dipping on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares rose in higher turnover on Friday but analysts said the stronger selling after price-fixing signalled a slight fall or flat market on Monday.
They said the market could then stabilise next week after having risen for much of September.

"We could have a slight dip or a flat market on Monday but I don't think the market will fall (from the current 14,735.5 points) below 14,500 points next week," said Wojciech Kossuth, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.9 percent to 14,735.5 points and turnover rose 32.2 percent to 138.4 million zlotys ($49.4 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 72 to three with three stocks flat.

Analysts said Friday's news that food prices grew 1.3 percent in September's second third meant it was still possible that year-on-year inflation would end the month lower than 20 percent and possibly lay the ground for an interest-rate cut.
Analysts said top-gainer Bank Komunalny, up 9.8 percent, should soon be hit by profit-taking but that mass privatisation NFI units, down one percent, could rebound on Monday after their one-day fall.
